idiom_name: duck-typed __init__ parameters (typing.Protocol for the seam) + app factory
implementation_notes: Python needs no container: __init__(self, repo, clock) declares the collaborators, the caller passes them, and nothing further is required because there is no compiler-enforced type to satisfy. What replaces the classic injector is the composition root - an application factory, main, or a test fixture - optionally with typing.Protocol to name the seam; FastAPI's Depends callables and dependency-injector's containers are the framework-scale realizations when request-scoped resolution or a large graph justifies them.
pitfalls: Mutable default arguments (def __init__(self, deps={})) share state across instances - use None plus a local default.
Module-level singletons (an engine, client or logger created at import) recreate the hidden dependency the pattern removes.
Duck typing fails at call time, not at wiring time - keep Protocol type hints or add a start-up check.

variants.name: dependency-injector DeclarativeContainer + wiring
variants.implementation_notes: dependency-injector makes the injector a first-class object: a DeclarativeContainer lists providers (Factory, Singleton, Configuration) that model the graph, and the wiring feature injects them into functions, methods and module attributes through @inject plus Provide[...] markers - including as FastAPI Depends(...) arguments - while overriding supports test substitution (container.override). What replaces hand-wiring is the container plus its configuration providers. Use it when the graph is large, when configuration must drive construction, or when several entry points share one graph.
pitfalls: Providers are lazy: an unconfigured provider fails on first use unless container.check_dependencies() runs at start-up.
Wiring patches modules, so a typo in module paths silently skips injection - configure WiringConfiguration and warn_unresolved.

variants.name: FastAPI Depends callables with per-request caching
variants.implementation_notes: FastAPI supplies a per-request injector: endpoint functions and their dependencies declare callables with Depends(), and FastAPI calls them, caches the result per request (use_cache), and supports generator dependencies whose yield separates setup from teardown. What replaces the container is the dependency-callable graph the framework resolves for each request; because the parameters are ordinary defaults, the same function can be unit-tested by calling it with explicit arguments. Idiomatic for HTTP layers, less suited to non-web graphs.
pitfalls: Depends factories run per request unless the dependency itself is cached or the object is created once at start-up (lifespan/state).
Calling a Depends-parameterised function directly in tests requires passing the dependency explicitly, otherwise the default marker object is used.
